newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares edge up in festive trade.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares edge up in festive trade.

text.p: Share prices on the Delhi Stock Exchange opened higher, in a special "moorat" trading session to mark the start of Hindu New Year, brokers said.
"Share prices have gone slightly higher because traders like to open their books with buying orders," said a Delhi stock broker who asked not to be identified.
Share prices rose on speculative buying by traders and investors, brokers said.
The bourse's benchmark index was 1.74 points higher at 696.22 after first 30 minutes of trade.
Moorat trade is held on the festival day of Diwali to mark the start of the Hindu New year.
Reliance Industries quoted 1.25 rupees higher at 187.25.
TISCO edged up 1.05 rupees to 168.75 rupees on speculative buying, brokers said.
State Bank of India was 0.20 rupee higher at 219.80, while Larsen and Toubro edged up by 2.75 rupees to 224.0.
